question.worked_solution:
To find ${f}^{-1}(x),$ we start by replacing $f(x)$ with $y:$

$$
y=-\frac{2x-5}{x-4}
$$

Now, interchanging $x$ and $y$ gives

$$
x=-\frac{2y-5}{y-4}.
$$

Then, we make $y$ the subject of the equation, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =-\frac{2y-5}{y-4} \\ -x & =\frac{2y-5}{y-4} \\ -x(y-4) & =2y-5 \\ -xy+4x & =2y-5 \\ 4x+5 & =xy+2y \\ 4x+5 & =y(x+2) \\ y & =\frac{4x+5}{x+2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the inverse function is 

$$
{f}^{-1}(x)=\frac{4x+5}{x+2}.
$$
